sentences.en: There is no God but Allah, and Muhammad is his messenger.
sentences.zh: 万物非主，唯有真主，穆罕默德是主的使者。

sentences.en: So runs the profession of faith familiar to some two billion people worldwide.
sentences.zh: 这句信仰宣言，全世界约有二十亿人耳熟能详。

sentences.en: But who was Muhammad?
sentences.zh: 但穆罕默德究竟是谁？

sentences.en: Where did he come from?
sentences.zh: 他从哪里来？

sentences.en: When did he live?
sentences.zh: 他生活在什么时代？

sentences.en: And what can we as historians know about him?
sentences.zh: 作为历史学家，我们又能了解他多少呢？

sentences.en: Tom Holland, difficult questions, but a fascinating subject.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰，这些问题很难，但这个主题非常迷人。

sentences.en: It's such a fascinating subject, and it's one that I spent about five years of my life wrestling with.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个迷人的主题，我花了大约五年时间来钻研它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And to be honest, it was so challenging.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这非常有挑战性。

sentences.en: It was kind of challenging intellectually, but also challenging because, of course, when you're writing about Muhammad, it's not like you're studying Nero or Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 在智力上这是一种挑战，但更具挑战性的是，当你书写穆罕默德时，这与研究尼禄或亚历山大大帝完全不同。

sentences.en: You're studying someone who is incredibly important to, as you said, two billion people.
sentences.zh: 你研究的是一个对你所说的二十亿人来说极其重要的人物。

sentences.en: So you are dealing with very, very profound issues.
sentences.zh: 所以你处理的是非常、非常深刻的问题。

sentences.en: And so I felt slightly tense about returning to this subject, I've got to say.
sentences.zh: 不得不说，重回这个主题让我感到有些紧张。

sentences.en: But I think it's incredibly worth doing because I think it is fascinating in and of itself,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这非常值得，因为它本身就引人入胜，

sentences.en: but also because I think it raises really interesting questions about the relationship of history to belief, to the dimension of the supernatural, to all kinds of things like that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它提出了关于历史与信仰、超自然维度以及诸如此类事物之间关系的非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: So really, I mean, the idea that we're going to do this in under an hour seems optimistic, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以说实话，要在不到一小时的时间里完成这个话题，我觉得有点过于乐观了。

sentences.en: But I think we should try and do our beSt.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们应该尽力而为。

sentences.en: We should do our beSt.
sentences.zh: 我们应该尽力而为。

sentences.en: I mean, what's interesting is obviously Muhammad is clearly one of the, you know, two, three, four people who have most shaped the course of human history.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，穆罕默德显然是塑造人类历史进程的二、三、四个人物之一。

sentences.en: I mean, if you, if we.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你，如果我们……

sentences.en: Did you, there was a book that was kind of like the hundred greatest, the hundred most influential people in history.
sentences.zh: 你有没有看过那本关于历史上百大最具影响力人物的书？

sentences.en: Did you have that?
sentences.zh: 你有那本书吗？

sentences.en: Was he number one?
sentences.zh: 他是第一名吗？

sentences.en: He was number one.
sentences.zh: 他是第一名。

sentences.en: And it was, it was kind of slightly mad book because I remember it had the Earl of Oxford.
sentences.zh: 那本书有点疯狂，因为我记得里面提到了牛津伯爵。

sentences.en: He, the guy who wrote it was convincing Earl of Oxford.
sentences.zh: 写那本书的人是个坚定的牛津伯爵支持者。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: I did a similar exercise when I was at school, you know, when I was about 12.
sentences.zh: 我上学时也做过类似的练习，大概12岁的时候。

sentences.en: We had to rank the 10 top people in history.
sentences.zh: 我们必须给历史上的前十名人物排名。

sentences.en: Do you know who mine was?
sentences.zh: 你知道我选的是谁吗？

sentences.en: James Callaghan.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·卡拉汉。

sentences.en: No, it's Martin Luther.
sentences.zh: 不，是马丁·路德。

sentences.en: That would appeal to you.
sentences.zh: 那倒是挺符合你的口味。

sentences.en: Anyway, this is a bit of a sidetrack.
sentences.zh: 总之，这有点跑题了。

sentences.en: Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德。

sentences.en: So obviously neither of us are MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 显然我们俩都不是穆斯林。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we're approaching this, it should be said at the outset for Muslim listeners.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们必须在开头就向穆斯林听众说明我们的立场。

sentences.en: Because we are approaching this from the perspective of Western non-believing historians, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 因为我们是从西方非信徒历史学家的角度来探讨这个问题的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I remember when I began looking at this, I kind of felt, well, I'm neutral because I don't believe this.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得刚开始研究时，我曾觉得，嗯，我是中立的，因为我不信这个。

sentences.en: But of course, my position of non-belief is not a neutral position at all.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我的非信徒立场根本不是中立的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the assumptions that I bring, you know, I assume that an angel did not speak to Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 我所持的假设，比如，我假设天使并没有对穆罕默德说话。

sentences.en: I assume that the Quran is not of divine origin.
sentences.zh: 我假设《古兰经》并非源自神启。

sentences.en: And therefore, my understanding, I'm sure your understanding of Muhammad is predicated on that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我的理解，我相信你对穆罕默德的理解，都是基于这些假设的。

sentences.en: But of course, that's not a neutral perspective at all.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这绝不是一个中立的视角。

sentences.en: So I think it's important to flag that up before we start.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在开始之前指出这一点很重要。

sentences.en: There are a lot of very respected scholars of early Islam who are not themselves MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 有很多受人尊敬的早期伊斯兰学者，他们自己并不是穆斯林。

sentences.en: I mean, we'll probably be talking about some of them later in the program.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后可能会在节目中谈到他们中的一些人。

sentences.en: So people who are fascinated by the history of Arabia and by the way in which Islam spread from its beginnings, you know, across the Mediterranean world,
sentences.zh: 所以，那些对阿拉伯历史以及伊斯兰教从其发源地传播到地中海世界的方式着迷的人，

sentences.en: across the Asian world and so on.
sentences.zh: 传播到亚洲世界等等。

sentences.en: But they're not necessarily themselves MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 但他们本人未必是穆斯林。

sentences.en: So I think you can reasonably want to talk and write about it without being a believer yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，即使不是信徒，也可以合理地想要谈论和书写它。

sentences.en: Anyway, listeners will be the judge of that, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 总之，我想听众们会对此做出评判的。

sentences.en: So why don't we start, since it's such fascinatingly sort of mysterious but also contentious territory,
sentences.zh: 既然这是一个如此迷人、神秘且充满争议的领域，我们为什么不开始呢？

sentences.en: why don't we start by you giving us a short kind of rundown for listeners who aren't familiar with the material of the traditional account of the life of Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 你能不能先为那些不熟悉相关资料的听众，简要概述一下关于穆罕默德生平的传统叙事？

sentences.en: So what, you know, if I go into an encyclopedia, what am I going to find about Muhammad's life?
sentences.zh: 如果我去查百科全书，关于穆罕默德的生平，我会找到什么？

sentences.en: So the context is the seventh Christian century beginning of it's the context is a world where the Near East is divided between the two great superpowers of Persia and Rome.
sentences.zh: 背景是公元七世纪，也就是基督纪元，当时近东被波斯和罗马这两个超级大国瓜分。

sentences.en: Rome, of course, now ruled from Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 当然，当时的罗马由君士坦丁堡统治。

sentences.en: Muhammad is born in a city called Mecca, which lies in an area of the Arabian Peninsula called the Hejaz, a thousand miles from the Roman frontier in Palestine.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德出生在麦加，位于阿拉伯半岛的汉志地区，距离巴勒斯坦的罗马边境有一千英里远。

sentences.en: He is a merchant.
sentences.zh: 他是一名商人。

sentences.en: He is married to a woman who is herself a merchant.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一位同样是商人的女性为妻。

sentences.en: He acts as her agent.
sentences.zh: 他担任她的代理人。

sentences.en: And he comes to the age of 40 and 40 in antiquity is the it's the age where you have your midlife crisis.
sentences.zh: 到了40岁，在古代，这就是你经历中年危机的年纪。

sentences.en: And Muhammad has perhaps the most epical midlife crisis in history when he starts hearing voices.
sentences.zh: 而穆罕默德经历的可能是历史上最史诗般的中年危机，他开始听到声音。

sentences.en: And this unsettles him because hearing voices in Mecca where he's growing up is potentially a mark that you've been seduced by a demon.
sentences.zh: 这让他感到不安，因为在他成长的麦加，听到声音可能意味着你被恶魔诱惑了。

sentences.en: But he gets reassured that actually he's being addressed by an angel.
sentences.zh: 但他得到保证，实际上是天使在对他说话。

sentences.en: And he is being hailed as the last of the prophets, the seal of the prophets.
sentences.zh: 他被誉为最后的先知，封印先知。

sentences.en: And he stands in a line of descent going back through Jesus, through Moses, all the way to Adam.
sentences.zh: 他站在一条传承线上，通过耶稣、摩西，一直追溯到亚当。

sentences.en: And his revelations are essentially the last chance that humanity has to live according to God's rules.
sentences.zh: 他的启示本质上是人类按照上帝规则生活的最后机会。

sentences.en: So Muhammad starts to say this.
sentences.zh: 于是穆罕默德开始宣扬这些。

sentences.en: Lots of people in Mecca think he's mad.
sentences.zh: 麦加的许多人认为他疯了。

sentences.en: But some don't.
sentences.zh: 但也有人不然。

sentences.en: Among them is Cardajah, his wife, and various other people start to rally around him.
sentences.zh: 其中包括他的妻子卡迪彻，以及其他开始聚集在他周围的人。

sentences.en: Cardajah dies, but Muhammad continues with his prophetic mission.
sentences.zh: 卡迪彻去世了，但穆罕默德继续他的先知使命。

sentences.en: And in time, hostility to his growing number of followers becomes such that he and his followers are forced to emigrate,
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，对他日益增多的追随者的敌意变得如此强烈，以至于他和他的追随者被迫移民，

sentences.en: to undergo what in Greek is an exodus and in Arabic is a hijra.
sentences.zh: 经历了一场在希腊语中称为“出埃及”，在阿拉伯语中称为“希吉拉”的迁徙。

sentences.en: And they go to a town called Yathrib.
sentences.zh: 他们去了雅特里布镇。

sentences.en: So that's modern day Medina.
sentences.zh: 也就是今天的麦地那。

sentences.en: Well, because it comes to be called, so Medina is a city, it comes to be called the city of the prophet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为它后来被称为麦地那，这是一座城市，被称为先知之城。

sentences.en: And in Medina, Muhammad essentially, guided by these divine revelations, sets up a community, a state.
sentences.zh: 在麦地那，穆罕默德在这些神圣启示的引导下，建立了一个社区，一个国家。

sentences.en: He takes over the running of the city.
sentences.zh: 他接管了城市的管理。

sentences.en: He expels those or slaughters those who do not subscribe to his teachings and his revelations.
sentences.zh: 他驱逐或杀戮了那些不认同他的教义和启示的人。

sentences.en: He defeats the Meccans and by treaty, he is allowed back into Mecca.
sentences.zh: 他击败了麦加人，并通过条约获准重返麦加。

sentences.en: And when he comes into Mecca, he topples the huge number of idols that exist everywhere.
sentences.zh: 当他进入麦加时，他推倒了到处存在的众多偶像。

sentences.en: And he establishes Mecca, which reaches back to the beginning of time.
sentences.zh: 他确立了麦加的地位，其历史可以追溯到时间的开端。

sentences.en: It's been a holy place since the origins of time.
sentences.zh: 自创世之初，它就是一个圣地。

sentences.en: It's a shrine that was established by Abraham and his son Ishmael right back in the beginnings of time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由亚伯拉罕和他的儿子易斯马仪在时间之初建立的神龛。

sentences.en: And Medina and Mecca are consecrated as these two cities that are hallowed by the role that they play in the life of the prophet.
sentences.zh: 麦地那和麦加被奉为两座圣城，因为它们在先知的生平中扮演了神圣的角色。

sentences.en: He dies, but his followers then take his message out into the world and inspired by these revelations that in time will be bundled together to form a single Quran,
sentences.zh: 他去世了，但他的追随者将他的信息带向世界，并受到这些启示的启发，这些启示最终被汇编成一部《古兰经》，

sentences.en: a single text of revelations.
sentences.zh: 一部单一的启示文本。

sentences.en: People who come to be known as Muslims swallow the Persian Empire whole, dismember a huge chunk of the Roman Empire, spread westwards to the Atlantic,
sentences.zh: 后来被称为穆斯林的人们吞并了波斯帝国，肢解了罗马帝国的一大块，向西传播到大西洋，

sentences.en: spread eastwards as far as the gates of China.
sentences.zh: 向东传播到中国边境。

sentences.en: And the result is the Muslim world that we have today.
sentences.zh: 结果就是我们今天所看到的穆斯林世界。

sentences.en: Yeah, very good.
sentences.zh: 好，非常好。

sentences.en: And so that is why, obviously, he could be voted the most influential human being who's ever lived.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么他会被评为有史以来最具影响力的人类。

sentences.en: Well, that was a bravura performance, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那真是一场精彩的表演，汤姆。

sentences.en: So we're talking a life that runs from about 570 to 632 or so, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是一个大约从570年到632年左右的生平。

sentences.en: Those are the conventional dates, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 这些是传统的日期，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: But those dates are inevitably contested.
sentences.zh: 但这些日期不可避免地受到质疑。

sentences.en: Because there are all kinds of historical questions that surround this narrative.
sentences.zh: 因为围绕这个叙事存在各种历史问题。

sentences.en: So we have a question from Diogo Morgado, who asks, what can be ascertained with some confidence about Muhammad's life?
sentences.zh: 我们有一个来自迪奥戈·莫尔加多的问题，他问，关于穆罕默德的生平，有什么是可以比较确定地查证的？

sentences.en: And that's a question to which there is a whole range of answers.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有各种答案的问题。

sentences.en: And at one extreme, you have people who say that the traditional accounts can be completely trusted.
sentences.zh: 在一个极端，有人说传统叙事完全可以信任。

sentences.en: And at the other end, you have people who say that basically we can't know anything about him.
sentences.zh: 而在另一个极端，有人说基本上我们对他一无所知。

sentences.en: In fact, there are even some who argue that he didn't even exiSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，甚至有人认为他根本不存在。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that, essentially, if we want a narrative account of Muhammad's life,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，本质上，如果我们想要穆罕默德生平的叙事记录，

sentences.en: we're dependent on texts that were first written down, or at least surviving texts that were written down.
sentences.zh: 我们依赖的是首次写下的文本，或者至少是幸存下来的写下的文本。

sentences.en: They date to about two centuries after the lifetime of Muhammad himself.
sentences.zh: 它们可以追溯到穆罕默德本人去世后大约两个世纪。

sentences.en: This is like Ibn Ishaq, is it?
sentences.zh: 这是指伊本·伊斯哈格，对吗？

sentences.en: Eighth century or so?
sentences.zh: 八世纪左右？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a guy called Ibn Ishaq who lives at the end of the eighth century.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个叫伊本·伊斯哈格的人，生活在八世纪末。

sentences.en: And he gets kind of redacted by a guy called Ibn Hissam.
sentences.zh: 他被一个叫伊本·希沙姆的人修订了。

sentences.en: And that's the version that we have.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们拥有的版本。

sentences.en: That's the earliest kind of narrative account.
sentences.zh: 那是最早的叙事记录。

sentences.en: So the question is, what is the relationship of those accounts of his life to the historical Muhammad?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，这些关于他生平的记录与历史上的穆罕默德之间是什么关系？

sentences.en: But there are fragments, aren't there, from the time.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些来自那个时代的片段，不是吗？

sentences.en: So I've got a couple of them here.
sentences.zh: 我这里有几个。

sentences.en: There's a Syriac fragment from 636.
sentences.zh: 有一个636年的叙利亚语片段。

sentences.en: Many villages were ruined with killing by the Arabs of Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 许多村庄被穆罕默德的阿拉伯人杀戮而毁坏。

sentences.en: So that's from within the sort of Roman world.
sentences.zh: 那是来自罗马世界内部的记录。

sentences.en: There's a guy called Thomas the Presbyter who, again, mentions the Arabs of Muhammad, 640.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫托马斯长老的人，也提到了穆罕默德的阿拉伯人，时间是640年。

sentences.en: And then the most famous one is from the 660s.
sentences.zh: 然后最著名的一个来自660年代。

sentences.en: So we're talking about, what's that, about 30 years after Muhammad conventionally is said to have died.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是，那是穆罕默德传统上被认为去世后大约30年。

sentences.en: Now, this is by an Armenian bishop.
sentences.zh: 这是由一位亚美尼亚主教写的。

sentences.en: And he tells the story.
sentences.zh: 他讲述了这个故事。

sentences.en: The sons of Ishmael.
sentences.zh: 易斯马仪的后代。

sentences.en: There's a guy whose name was Muhammad, a merchant.
sentences.zh: 有一个名字叫穆罕默德的人，是个商人。

sentences.en: He taught them to recognize the God of Abraham, especially because he was learned and informed in the history of Moses.
sentences.zh: 他教导他们认识亚伯拉罕的上帝，特别是因为他博学且了解摩西的历史。

sentences.en: He told them, love only the God of Abraham.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他们，只爱亚伯拉罕的上帝。

sentences.en: Go and seize the land which God gave you to your father, Abraham.
sentences.zh: 去夺取上帝赐予你们祖先亚伯拉罕的土地。

sentences.en: No one will be able to resist you in battle because God is with you.
sentences.zh: 没有人能在战斗中抵挡你们，因为上帝与你们同在。

sentences.en: So those are sources that appear to allude to the Muhammad that we know, but they're written from outside the Muslim tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以这些来源似乎都提到了我们所知的穆罕默德，但它们是从穆斯林传统之外书写的。

sentences.en: So these are guys who are maybe hundreds of miles away.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人可能在几百英里之外。

sentences.en: There is one that seems to be written during Muhammad's own lifetime.
sentences.zh: 有一个似乎是在穆罕默德生前写的。

sentences.en: And so if that's the case, then Muhammad is the only founder of a great religious tradition of whom that can be said.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，那么穆罕默德就是唯一一位有此记载的伟大宗教传统的创始人。

sentences.en: Well, that's a fascinating point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一个迷人的观点。

sentences.en: So in other words, Muhammad is far from Muhammad being, well, OK, we can talk about the sources about Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，穆罕默德远非……好吧，我们可以谈论关于穆罕默德的来源。

sentences.en: But what's clear, he's not unusual.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见，他并不特殊。

sentences.en: I mean, Jesus, there are virtually no sources from the life of Jesus, I think.
sentences.zh: 我是说，耶稣，几乎没有任何关于耶稣生平的来源，我想。

sentences.en: No, there are no sources from Jesus' life.
sentences.zh: 不，没有关于耶稣生平的来源。

sentences.en: But there are sources.
sentences.zh: 但确实有来源。

sentences.en: So we have Paul's letters that are written a decade or so after.
sentences.zh: 我们有保罗的书信，写于十年左右之后。

sentences.en: And then the Gospels are written a few decades after that.
sentences.zh: 然后福音书是在那之后的几十年写的。

sentences.en: The problem is, is that we don't have the equivalent of Gospels.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们没有相当于福音书的东西。

sentences.en: We don't have the equivalent of narrative lives of the prophet until much later.
sentences.zh: 直到很久以后，我们才有了相当于先知叙事生平的东西。

sentences.en: So it would be analogous to the kind of Gnostic Gospels that are being written around 200 AD.
sentences.zh: 所以这类似于公元200年左右写成的那些诺斯替福音书。

sentences.en: And no one looks at those and thinks that they are a kind of authentic account of what happened in first century AD Judea.
sentences.zh: 没人会看着那些书，认为它们是对公元一世纪犹地亚所发生之事的真实记录。

sentences.en: So that's the question.
sentences.zh: 所以问题就在这里。

sentences.en: But having said that, yes, we do have these kind of early sources that clearly, I mean, it seems to me, I can't imagine how anyone really can argue that Muhammad didn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，是的，我们确实有这些早期的文献来源，在我看来，我无法想象还有谁能真正争辩说穆罕默德不存在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He clearly did.
sentences.zh: 他显然是存在的。

sentences.en: These early texts, I mean, this is pretty solid evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 这些早期文献，我的意思是，这是相当有力的证据。

sentences.en: And as I say, we have this one source called the Doctrina Jacobi, and it describes how Saracens, Arabs, led by a prophet, have invaded Roman Palestine and defeated the Romans.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们有一个名为《雅各的教义》（Doctrina Jacobi）的文献来源，它描述了撒拉逊人（阿拉伯人）在一位先知的带领下，如何入侵罗马治下的巴勒斯坦并击败了罗马人。

sentences.en: And it's hard to think who this is a reference to.
sentences.zh: 很难想象这指的是谁。

sentences.en: It doesn't name Muhammad, but it's hard to think who this is referring to, if not Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 它没有指名道姓说是穆罕默德，但如果不是指穆罕默德，很难想象还能指谁。

sentences.en: But there is a problem, and there are two problems with it.
sentences.zh: 但这里有个问题，确切地说是两个问题。

sentences.en: One is that it's dated to 634, and the tradition, as you said, is that Muhammad dies in 632.
sentences.zh: 一是它的成书日期是634年，而正如你所说，传统认为穆罕默德死于632年。

sentences.en: So how do we square that?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何协调这一点呢？

sentences.en: The other is that it describes Muhammad leading an invasion, and the Muslim tradition is absolutely clear that he did not do that, that he dies before the invasion of Palestine,
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，它描述了穆罕默德领导了一场入侵，而穆斯林传统非常明确地表示他并没有这样做，他在对巴勒斯坦的入侵之前就已经去世了，

sentences.en: which is the first target.
sentences.zh: 而巴勒斯坦是他们的第一个目标。

sentences.en: There's probably a good way of answering that, though, isn't there, Tom?
sentences.zh: 不过，汤姆，应该有一个很好的解释方法，对吧？

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, one good way of answering it would be he's still alive and he's leading the invasion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，一个很好的解释是，他当时还活着，并且正在领导那场入侵。

sentences.en: But another one would be that the guy who's, what's it called, the teaching of Jacob or whatever, that Jacob or whoever it is, is a Jacob who's writing it.
sentences.zh: 但另一种解释是，那个写下《雅各的教义》的人，那个雅各或者不管是谁，他只是个写书的雅各。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Is that his name?
sentences.zh: 那是他的名字吗？

sentences.en: It's complicated.
sentences.zh: 这很复杂。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, whoever it is.
sentences.zh: 总之，不管他是谁。

sentences.en: I mean, who cares who it is?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁在乎他是谁呢？

sentences.en: Whoever he is, he's repeating a garbled story that he's heard in an age when information travels slowly and incompletely.
sentences.zh: 无论他是谁，他都在重复一个道听途说的故事，那是一个信息传播缓慢且不完整的时代。

sentences.en: And he might just have got it wrong or his interlocutor might have got it wrong.
sentences.zh: 他可能只是弄错了，或者他的讲述者弄错了。

sentences.en: I think there's a more interesting explanation, which is that the person who, the prophet, the biblical figure who is named more than any other in the Quran is Moses.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一个更有趣的解释，那就是在《古兰经》中被提及次数最多的先知和圣经人物是摩西。

sentences.en: And I've already mentioned that the hijra, the exile, the exodus.
sentences.zh: 我已经提到了“希吉拉”（迁徙），即流亡，即出埃及。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what Moses does.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是摩西所做的事。

sentences.en: He leads his people from Egypt to the promised land.
sentences.zh: 他带领他的人民从埃及前往应许之地。

sentences.en: And that's essentially what Muhammad does when he leads his people from Mecca to Medina.
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是穆罕默德带领他的人民从麦加迁往麦地那时所做的事情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The other thing that for which Moses is famous is that he dies before the children of Israel enter the promised land.
sentences.zh: 摩西出名的另一件事是，他在以色列子民进入应许之地前就去世了。

sentences.en: And essentially what this, this is a problem if you were casting Muhammad as, you know, the new Moses, which I think is basically what's going on.
sentences.zh: 本质上，如果你把穆罕默德塑造成“新摩西”，这就会成为一个问题，而我认为这正是当时正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So you can see how that tradition would be erased and you start to construct a tradition in which Muhammad is described as like Moses dying before his people enter the promised land.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出，那种传统是如何被抹去，并开始构建一种新的传统，即穆罕默德像摩西一样，在人民进入应许之地前就去世了。

sentences.en: And this focuses attention on something that also that's very interesting, which is that the it's clear that Palestine, Jerusalem, the Holy Land,
sentences.zh: 这让人们关注到另一件非常有趣的事情，那就是很明显，巴勒斯坦、耶路撒冷、圣地，

sentences.en: the sense of of belonging to this biblical tradition going back through Jesus, through Moses to Abraham is incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 那种通过耶稣、摩西一直追溯到亚伯拉罕的圣经传统归属感，是极其重要的。

sentences.en: And the fact that Palestine is the first target of the invasions doesn't seem to be a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 而且巴勒斯坦是入侵的首要目标，这似乎并非巧合。

sentences.en: So I think that what happens is that if you look at these early sources,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为发生的情况是，如果你审视这些早期文献，

sentences.en: you can kind of work out a way in which there is an emphasis on the Holy Land that in due course comes to fade because the Arab empire comes to embrace a vast range of territories.
sentences.zh: 你可以理出一条线索，即当时对圣地的强调，随着阿拉伯帝国版图的不断扩张，这种强调在后来逐渐淡化了。

sentences.en: And essentially what begins perhaps as a movement that is more Jewish, that is more ethnocentric, that is more focused on a holy land, comes to be more Christian,
sentences.zh: 本质上，最初可能是一场更偏向犹太教、更以民族为中心、更关注圣地的运动，后来变得更基督教化，

sentences.en: comes to be more universalizing.
sentences.zh: 变得更具普世性。

sentences.en: And what emerges as Islam, and I think that Islam is not kind of something that's served up on a plate by Muhammad to his followers and they then take it out.
sentences.zh: 而作为伊斯兰教出现的东西，我认为它并不是穆罕默德现成地端给追随者，然后他们就直接拿去用的东西。

sentences.en: I think it's something that emerges over the course of the Arab conquests and the decades that follow,
sentences.zh: 我认为它是随着阿拉伯征服及其后的几十年里逐渐形成的，

sentences.en: that it emerges to provide the new rulers of this vast empire with an explanation for why God has given them this empire and why they deserve to continue ruling it.
sentences.zh: 它的出现是为了给这个庞大帝国的新统治者提供一个解释：为什么上帝把这个帝国赐予了他们，以及为什么他们理应继续统治它。

sentences.en: Let's widen it out a bit because I think we should give a bit of a sense of context because I think we can understand Muhammad and that movement to Palestine and all the rest of it more completely if we understand what's going on.
sentences.zh: 让我们把话题拓宽一点，因为我认为我们应该提供一些背景，如果我们了解当时的情况，就能更全面地理解穆罕默德、那场针对巴勒斯坦的运动以及其他一切。

sentences.en: Quite often I think you'll read in books will say, you know, it's Rome and it's Persia and then suddenly in the mid 7th century, almost out of nowhere, out of the desert,
sentences.zh: 你经常会在书中读到，你知道，那是罗马和波斯，然后突然在七世纪中期，几乎是凭空出现，从沙漠中，

sentences.en: these guys who no one knew about erupt with this new message of Islam that has just come out of nowhere and it's this great shock and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 这些没人知道的家伙带着伊斯兰教的新信息爆发出来，这简直是凭空出现，是一个巨大的冲击，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I was always thinking that's not a very persuasive or indeed compelling account of what happened because I think what happened is actually much more interesting.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为这并不是一个非常有说服力或令人信服的解释，因为我认为实际发生的事情要有趣得多。

sentences.en: So you've got, I mean, if you think about these two superpowers.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想想这两个超级大国。

sentences.en: So you studied this, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 你研究过这个，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我研究过。

sentences.en: So you studied this.
sentences.zh: 所以你研究过这个。

sentences.en: So that was what, 80s?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候，80年代？
90年代，90年代。

sentences.en: So what were you studying?
sentences.zh: 那你当时在研究什么？

sentences.en: What were you being told?
sentences.zh: 你当时被告知了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I did a course that was famous at Oxford because it was the first course where you didn't have to, where you were allowed to read things in translation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我修了一门在牛津很有名的课程，因为那是第一门允许你阅读翻译文本的课程。

sentences.en: So it was a course called The Near East in the Age of Justinian and Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 那门课叫《查士丁尼和穆罕默德时代的近东》。

sentences.en: And it's part of going to Oxford kind of history law, not that that's saying very much to people who don't care about Oxford history who listen to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是牛津历史系课程的一部分，虽然这对那些不关心牛津历史的播客听众来说没什么意义。

sentences.en: But it was the first course.
sentences.zh: 但它是第一门这样的课程。

sentences.en: Previously, you could never do stuff at Oxford if you couldn't read the original sources.
sentences.zh: 以前在牛津，如果你不能阅读原始文献，你就永远无法研究这些课题。

sentences.en: And a great Russian history of Byzantium, I think it was, Dmitry Obelensky, said, you know,
sentences.zh: 一位伟大的俄罗斯拜占庭历史学家，我想是德米特里·奥博连斯基，他说，你知道，

sentences.en: this is completely unreasonable because no one's going to arrive at Oxford and be able to read like Armenian, medieval Armenian or something.
sentences.zh: 这完全不合理，因为没人会在来到牛津时就能读懂亚美尼亚语、中世纪亚美尼亚语之类的语言。

sentences.en: So they agreed that you could do this course.
sentences.zh: 所以他们同意你可以修这门课。

sentences.en: And so you did this course, which was Justinian and Muhammad and the world of, you know, the Near East at the time of the fall of, you know, the empire in the West has fallen.
sentences.zh: 于是你修了这门课，讲的是查士丁尼和穆罕默德，以及当时近东的世界，你知道，西方帝国已经灭亡了。

sentences.en: Rome is becoming Byzantium.
sentences.zh: 罗马正在变成拜占庭。

sentences.en: You know, there's going to become this new Islamic world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即将出现这个新的伊斯兰世界。

sentences.en: And what I learned, so for me, it was one of the most interesting, and it's why I really wanted to do this subject, actually,
sentences.zh: 我所学到的，对我来说，这是最有趣的课题之一，这也是我为什么真的想研究这个学科，实际上，

sentences.en: because it's one of the most interesting intellectual adventures, if I can call it that, that I've kind of been on.
sentences.zh: 因为如果可以这么说的话，这是我所经历过的最有趣的智力冒险之一。

sentences.en: Because, of course, you first read the traditional accounts of Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，你首先读到的是关于穆罕默德的传统叙述。

sentences.en: And then there's this whole historiography, which even then was incredibly, still, you know, very controversial.
sentences.zh: 然后是整个史学研究，即使在当时，它也仍然非常有争议。

sentences.en: So there was a guy called John Wandsborough, American scholar of Islam, and we read that.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫约翰·万斯伯勒的美国伊斯兰学者，我们读过他的著作。

sentences.en: And he basically said, you know, the traditional version is wrong.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，你知道，传统版本是错误的。

sentences.en: I mean, you'll know all this, Tom, that the Koran, that Islam is a later creation than everyone thinks, that the Arab conquest kind of happened firSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，你肯定知道这一切，即《古兰经》，即伊斯兰教是一个比大家想象的更晚的产物，阿拉伯征服是先发生的。

sentences.en: And that it emerges out of the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 它是从中东产生的。

sentences.en: And that, yes, exactly, that it emerges out of, you know, once they've got the Arab empire, then they need to develop a creed for it, basically.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，它产生于，你知道，一旦他们建立了阿拉伯帝国，他们基本上就需要为它发展出一套信条。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm really simplifying it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我真的在简化它。

sentences.en: And then two of his students, as you will know, Patricia Croner and Michael Cook, took that on, and it came up with this argument called Hagarism, where they basically argued that,
sentences.zh: 然后正如你所知，他的两名学生，帕特里夏·克罗内和迈克尔·库克，继承了这一观点，并提出了一个名为“哈加里派”（Hagarism）的论点，他们基本上认为，

sentences.en: you know, Islam had begun as a Jewish messianic movement, and then developed a kind of Arab component later on when they decided to ditch the Jewishness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伊斯兰教最初是一场犹太弥赛亚运动，后来在他们决定抛弃犹太教色彩时，才发展出了一种阿拉伯成分。

sentences.en: But that was very controversial, even in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 但这在90年代也非常有争议。

sentences.en: I mean, I think when I was studying it, we read that, but then to kind of slightly, it had already been slightly repudiated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我在学习的时候读过它，但后来它已经被稍微否定了。

sentences.en: The authors themselves had said, well, actually, maybe there was a Mohammed and there was a, you know, the Koran.
sentences.zh: 作者本人也说过，嗯，实际上，也许确实有一个穆罕默德，也确实有《古兰经》。

sentences.en: So, and I think actually, as far as I can tell from the historiography, and I'm not an expert in this by any means, people have found engravings and so on, inscriptions,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为实际上，据我所知，从史学研究来看，我绝不是这方面的专家，人们已经发现了雕刻等等，铭文，

sentences.en: there's more evidence than people thought for a historic Mohammed.
sentences.zh: 关于历史上的穆罕默德，证据比人们想象的要多。

sentences.en: Is that, would you agree with that?
sentences.zh: 你会同意这一点吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Well, I think, I mean, I think essentially what the process of the historiography is that you have these two very radical extremes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为，我的意思是，我认为史学研究的过程本质上是你有两个非常激进的极端。

sentences.en: Mohammed didn't exist, the Koran was compiled.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德不存在，《古兰经》是后来汇编的。

sentences.en: That's the Hagarism.
sentences.zh: 这就是“哈加里派”的观点。

sentences.en: Over the 7th and 8th century.
sentences.zh: 在七世纪和八世纪。

sentences.en: That's particularly the Wands preposition.
sentences.zh: 这主要是万斯伯勒的命题。

sentences.en: And then you had the traditional account in which Mecca is kind of the Dubai of its day, you know, spice trains and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后你有传统的叙述，其中麦加是当时那个时代的迪拜，你知道，香料贸易路线等等。

sentences.en: And there's a crisis for capitalism.
sentences.zh: 还有一场资本主义危机。

sentences.en: And basically, it's a 1970s, you know, back projection onto 7th century Arabia.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是20世纪70年代对七世纪阿拉伯世界的投射。

sentences.en: And I think that both of those have kind of fallen by the wayside.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两种观点都已经过时了。

sentences.en: But I think what's emerged is an attempt to situate Mohammed within the world of late antiquity as a holy man.
sentences.zh: 但我认为出现的是一种试图将穆罕默德置于古典时代晚期作为圣人的世界中。

sentences.en: And late antiquity is a period where...
sentences.zh: 而古典时代晚期是一个……

sentences.en: Yeah, rich and holy men.
sentences.zh: 是的，富有而神圣的人。

sentences.en: Very rich and holy men.
sentences.zh: 非常富有而神圣的人。

sentences.en: Rich and holy men.
sentences.zh: 富有而神圣的人。

sentences.en: But I'll tell you what we should say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但我告诉你我们应该说什么，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's rich and holy men because this is a world going through an astonishing trauma.
sentences.zh: 是富有而神圣的人，因为这是一个正在经历惊人创伤的世界。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Generally, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 通常是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有……

sentences.en: So for people who don't, who aren't familiar with this incredibly interesting period of late antiquity, you know, tax bases are collapsing.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些不熟悉这个极其有趣的古典时代晚期的人来说，你知道，税基正在崩溃。

sentences.en: Because of plague.
sentences.zh: 因为瘟疫。

sentences.en: There's been this massive plague in the 6th century.
sentences.zh: 六世纪发生过一场大规模的瘟疫。

sentences.en: This devastating plague that people say, you know, has killed a third half of the world.
sentences.zh: 这场毁灭性的瘟疫，人们说，你知道，杀死了世界三分之一甚至一半的人口。

sentences.en: Maybe exaggeration, but maybe in certain places not.
sentences.zh: 也许是夸张，但在某些地方可能并非如此。

sentences.en: Which I think only recently historians have really given the centrality it deserves.
sentences.zh: 我认为直到最近，历史学家才真正给予它应有的核心地位。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing about that relative to what's happening in Arabia is that it hits cities disproportionately.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，相对于阿拉伯地区正在发生的事情，有趣的是它对城市的影响不成比例。

sentences.en: And you have Arab accounts about it.
sentences.zh: 而且你有关于它的阿拉伯记载。

sentences.en: So the plague is described as arrows shot by the djinn.
sentences.zh: 所以瘟疫被描述为精灵射出的箭。

sentences.en: So a bit like, you know, Apollo raining arrows on the Greeks in the Iliad.
sentences.zh: 所以有点像，你知道，《伊利亚特》中阿波罗向希腊人降下箭雨。

sentences.en: But these arrows only hit you if you come out of the desert.
sentences.zh: 但这些箭只有当你从沙漠出来时才会射中你。

sentences.en: So perhaps there there's a kind of interesting clue to what's going on.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这里有一个关于正在发生什么的有趣线索。

sentences.en: That for the first time, there's this kind of, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是第一次，有这种，你知道，

sentences.en: the huge imbalance of population between those in the Vertile Crescent and those in the deserts beyond is starting to ease down.
sentences.zh: 肥沃月湾的人口与沙漠之外的人口之间的巨大失衡开始缓解。

sentences.en: And then you have the Great War on top of that.
sentences.zh: 然后在此之上还有一场大战。

sentences.en: Yeah, this massive war.
sentences.zh: 是的，这场大规模的战争。

sentences.en: So, I mean, what are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我们在谈论什么？

sentences.en: Rome and Persia have been the two superpowers for basically, what, 700 years?
sentences.zh: 罗马和波斯基本上是两个超级大国，有多久了，700年？

sentences.en: So they've divided that world between...
sentences.zh: 所以他们瓜分了那个世界……

sentences.en: It's 500 years, the Sassanians and the Romans.
sentences.zh: 萨珊王朝和罗马人有500年了。

sentences.en: Well, Persia more generally, though, in this space.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过在这个空间里，波斯更广泛一些。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的是的是的。

sentences.en: Going back even further.
sentences.zh: 追溯得更远。

sentences.en: So they launched this sort of, you know, 30 years war style from 602 to 628, I think it is, which seesaws incredibly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们发动了这种，你知道，三十年战争风格的战争，从602年到628年，我想是这样，局势极其动荡。

sentences.en: I mean, it's sort of Game of Thrones style war, which the Persians seem to carry all before them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种《权力的游戏》风格的战争，波斯人似乎所向披靡。

sentences.en: And they capture these provinces.
sentences.zh: 他们占领了这些省份。

sentences.en: Including Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 包括耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: Yeah, Egypt, Palestine, and so on, that have been central to the Roman world.
sentences.zh: 是的，埃及、巴勒斯坦等等，这些一直是罗马世界的中心。

sentences.en: And then Heraclius, this extraordinary Roman general, takes the reins of the...
sentences.zh: 然后希拉克略，这位非凡的罗马将军，接过了……

sentences.en: He's the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他是皇帝。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, he takes the reins of the empire.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，他接过了帝国的统治权。

sentences.en: And then he goes on these campaigns where he, you know, he spends winter on campaign, which is really sort of groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 然后他进行了这些战役，你知道，他在战役中度过冬天，这真的是开创性的。

sentences.en: And he basically casts the Persians back, reconquers all this territory.
sentences.zh: 他基本上把波斯人赶了回去，收复了所有这些领土。

sentences.en: And at that point, if everyone people often say, his biographies and people say, if only he died.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上，如果每个人，人们经常说，他的传记作者和人们说，如果他当时就死了。

sentences.en: If only he died right then, he would be remembered as one of the absolute all-time great Roman emperors.
sentences.zh: 如果他当时就死了，他会被铭记为有史以来最伟大的罗马皇帝之一。

sentences.en: But of course, he doesn't die.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他没有死。

sentences.en: And what happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Suddenly, these fellows will appear out in the desert.
sentences.zh: 突然，这些家伙出现在沙漠里。

sentences.en: And they take all the provinces that the Romans had captured back from the Persians.
sentences.zh: 他们夺取了罗马人从波斯人手中夺回的所有省份。

sentences.en: And so you will then read that the Arabs come and they defeat the Romans in Palestine.
sentences.zh: 所以你随后会读到阿拉伯人来了，他们在巴勒斯坦击败了罗马人。

sentences.en: But the question is, what are the Romans?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，什么是罗马人？

sentences.en: Because, you know, they've been kicked out for ages.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，他们已经被赶走很久了。

sentences.en: And the whole apparatus of Roman control has melted away.
sentences.zh: 罗马帝国的整个控制体系已经土崩瓦解了。

sentences.en: And what's also interesting is that both the Romans and the Persians are paying Arabs to essentially kind of serve as buffer zones along the borders.
sentences.zh: 同样有趣的是，罗马人和波斯人都在花钱雇佣阿拉伯人，让他们在边境充当缓冲地带。

sentences.en: So there's two regimes, aren't there, the Gassassanids and the Lachmids.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有两个政权，对吧，伽珊尼德人和拉赫姆人。

sentences.en: And because both empires are short of money, essentially they're franchising out the patrolling of the frontier to these Arabs.
sentences.zh: 由于两大帝国都缺钱，他们本质上是将边境巡逻的任务外包给了这些阿拉伯人。

sentences.en: When the Romans get kicked out of Palestine, those Arabs have no money coming in.
sentences.zh: 当罗马人被赶出巴勒斯坦时，那些阿拉伯人就失去了收入来源。

sentences.en: And this is exactly the period at which tradition places Mohammed and the emergence of this kind of huge army waiting to take over.
sentences.zh: 而这正是传统观点中穆罕默德出现的时期，也是那支准备接管政权的庞大军队崛起的时期。

sentences.en: Now, it's possible that essentially what you have in Palestine after the expulsion of the Persians is kind of like French Vietnam, you know, after the Second World War,
sentences.zh: 现在，有一种可能，即波斯人被驱逐后的巴勒斯坦，其状况就像二战后的法属越南一样，你知道的，

sentences.en: that the French are coming back in trying to resurrect their rule.
sentences.zh: 法国人试图回来重建他们的统治。

sentences.en: But essentially their prestige has been demolished.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，他们的威望已经荡然无存。

sentences.en: And there are very few kind of French troopers there.
sentences.zh: 而且那里的法国士兵也非常少。

sentences.en: And essentially what is cast by the later tradition as a kind of great invasion may just be a kind of slow implosion in which Arabs who previously had been employed as mercenaries essentially kind of move in and don't need the Romans and they just take it over.
sentences.zh: 后世传统将其描述为一场大入侵，但本质上可能只是一场缓慢的内爆，那些曾经被雇佣为雇佣兵的阿拉伯人，本质上是搬了进来，他们不再需要罗马人，于是直接接管了那里。

sentences.en: So it's possible that that is what is going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很有可能就是当时发生的事情。

sentences.en: But it's also true, isn't it, Tom, that there's much more interplay between the Arab world and the Roman and Persian worlds than people often think.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，阿拉伯世界与罗马和波斯世界之间的互动比人们通常认为的要多得多，这也是事实，不是吗？

sentences.en: So the common version, which is there's this sort of veil of sand behind which these guys have been lurking for hundreds of years and no one's cared about it.
sentences.zh: 通常的说法是，有一层沙幕，这些家伙在沙幕后潜伏了数百年，没人关心他们。

sentences.en: And suddenly they erupt and they're these incredible new forces, sort of like the Dothraki arriving in Westeros to go back to our Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 然后他们突然爆发，成为了一股不可思议的新力量，就像《权力的游戏》里多斯拉克人抵达维斯特洛一样。

sentences.en: But that's not really the case at all.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They've been trading with the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他们一直与罗马人有贸易往来。

sentences.en: They've been working for them.
sentences.zh: 他们一直为罗马人工作。

sentences.en: People have been traveling back and forth.
sentences.zh: 人们一直在往来穿梭。

sentences.en: I mean, they all knew.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们都知道。

sentences.en: And that's where the ideas, the religious ideas.
sentences.zh: 而思想，那些宗教思想，就是从那里来的。

sentences.en: I mean, there are Christians.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那里有基督徒。

sentences.en: There are Arab Christians, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 有阿拉伯基督徒，对吧？

sentences.en: There are.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: So this is over the past decades.
sentences.zh: 所以这是过去几十年的情况。

sentences.en: This has been the main focus of trying to understand who or what Mohammed might have been is to recognize, is to try and situate him in that world,
sentences.zh: 试图理解穆罕默德是谁或是什么，其核心焦点在于认识到这一点，即试图将他置于那个世界中，

sentences.en: in the world of Persia and Roman rivalry, but also a world that is absolutely teeming with Christian, with Jewish, even with Zoroastrian elements.
sentences.zh: 置于波斯与罗马竞争的世界中，同时也是一个充斥着基督教、犹太教，甚至琐罗亚斯德教元素的世界。

sentences.en: And perhaps, just perhaps, with traditions that have faded elsewhere, but are still current in the deserts beyond Palestine.
sentences.zh: 或许，仅仅是或许，还有一些在其他地方已经消逝，但在巴勒斯坦之外的沙漠中依然流行的传统。

sentences.en: Now, because if you look at the traditional accounts of Mohammed, these biographies that over the course of the ninth into the 10th century,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你看看关于穆罕默德的传统叙述，那些在9世纪到10世纪期间形成的传记，

sentences.en: they become more and more elaborate the further away you go.
sentences.zh: 你离那个时代越远，它们就变得越复杂。

sentences.en: So they're clearly being extraneous information is being added to it.
sentences.zh: 很明显，其中被添加了无关的信息。

sentences.en: A bit like Arthurian romances don't tell you anything really about the context of, you know, late Roman Britain or post-Roman Britain.
sentences.zh: 就像亚瑟王传奇并不能真正告诉你关于罗马帝国晚期或后罗马时代英国的背景一样。

sentences.en: So likewise, these biographies of Mohammed do not tell you very much about they don't they're not really grounded in a recognizable world of late antiquity.
sentences.zh: 同样，这些穆罕默德的传记并没有告诉你太多关于……它们并不是真正建立在可识别的古典时代晚期的世界之上。

sentences.en: You know, there's the odd Christian, there's the odd, you know, there's a tribe of Jews who get dealt with at Medina, there's kind of mentions of Heraclius, but by and large,
sentences.zh: 你知道，偶尔会有基督徒出现，偶尔会有在麦地那被处理的犹太部落，也会提到希拉克略，但总的来说，

sentences.en: it's not a world that is rich in mentions that we can recognize as being late antique.
sentences.zh: 那并不是一个充满我们能识别为古典时代晚期特征的世界。

sentences.en: So the fascination is to try and situate Mohammed in a context that makes sense of him as an early 7th century figure rather than as someone who has been constructed basically to explain things and to justify things that the Muslim rulers and indeed Muslims more generally in the later centuries need him to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，令人着迷的是，试图将穆罕默德置于一个能让他作为7世纪早期人物而不仅仅是一个为了解释和证明后世穆斯林统治者乃至一般穆斯林需要他做的事情而被构建出来的人物的情境中。

sentences.en: And so that's that's the challenge is do you do you jettison the Islamic tradition completely and do you only draw on, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，挑战在于，你是要完全抛弃伊斯兰传统，只利用那些，你知道的，

sentences.en: texts that originate within or in the decades after his life or are there elements within the Muslim tradition that you can you can draw on and construct a model for.
sentences.zh: 源于他生前或去世后几十年内的文本，还是说穆斯林传统中确实有一些元素可以让你利用并构建一个模型？

sentences.en: And and and there is really there is one there's one key question, I think, which really underlies this that the whole problem and it's only a problem for non-MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 而且，确实有一个关键问题，我认为，这实际上是整个问题的基础，而且这只是非穆斯林面临的问题。

sentences.en: So for Muslims, it's not a problem to explain where the Quran comes from.
sentences.zh: 对于穆斯林来说，解释《古兰经》的来源不是问题。

sentences.en: It comes from God.
sentences.zh: 它来自上帝。

sentences.en: That's the essence of what a Muslim believes.
sentences.zh: 这就是穆斯林信仰的核心。

sentences.en: But if you're not a Muslim, you have to explain how it was that where does the Quran come from?
sentences.zh: 但如果你不是穆斯林，你就必须解释《古兰经》究竟是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Um, the ones for a thesis that the Quran emerged over the 8th and 9th century has been conclusively disproved, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那种认为《古兰经》是在8世纪和9世纪才出现的论点，我认为已经被彻底推翻了。

sentences.en: I think it's clear that the Quran is associated with someone called Mohammed.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，《古兰经》与一个叫穆罕默德的人有关。

sentences.en: And although it takes time for it to be compiled, it's clear that there are prophetic utterances that together will constitute the Quran.
sentences.zh: 虽然它的编纂需要时间，但很明显，有一些先知性的言论共同构成了《古兰经》。

sentences.en: So therefore, the Quran does provide, I think, evidence for the kind of world in which the historical Mohammed was living.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为《古兰经》确实为历史上的穆罕默德所生活的世界提供了证据。

sentences.en: But of course, you still have to explain how and why it is that these these texts emerge.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你仍然必须解释这些文本是如何以及为什么出现的。

sentences.en: Well, Tom, why don't you do that after the break?
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，为什么不在休息之后再讲呢？

sentences.en: Well, because I just want to I just want to set up what that this is a problem, because there is no other account we have of where the Quran comes from,
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我只是想，我只是想说明这是一个问题，因为我们没有关于《古兰经》来源的其他记载，

sentences.en: except the traditional Muslim one.
sentences.zh: 除了传统的穆斯林版本。

sentences.en: And I remember being struck by what a problem this is for secular historians, where I went to an exhibition in the Metropolitan Museum in New York about Byzantium in early Islam.
sentences.zh: 我记得我曾被这对世俗历史学家来说是一个多么大的问题所震撼，当时我去纽约大都会艺术博物馆参观了一个关于拜占庭和早期伊斯兰教的展览。

sentences.en: And the the the the, you know, the labels, the the kind of counts in very, you know, the Byzantine rooms were all very secular.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拜占庭展厅里的标签，那些叙述，都非常世俗。

sentences.en: So the descriptions of Christian practices were not from a Christian point of view.
sentences.zh: 所以对基督教习俗的描述并非出自基督徒的视角。

sentences.en: It was very, very objective, very, very secular.
sentences.zh: 非常非常客观，非常非常世俗。

sentences.en: Then you got to the Islam room and there was a collection of early Korans and there was a kind of billboard talking about the Korans.
sentences.zh: 然后你到了伊斯兰展厅，那里收藏了一些早期的《古兰经》，还有一个关于《古兰经》的展板。

sentences.en: And it said the Koran was revealed, you know, the revelations that were given to Mohammed by by God and that came to him by the angel.
sentences.zh: 上面写着《古兰经》是启示，你知道的，是上帝通过天使传达给穆罕默德的启示。

sentences.en: And that was it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: There was no context.
sentences.zh: 没有任何背景。

sentences.en: There was no attempt to explain what this might mean for someone who doesn't believe in God or doesn't believe in angels or even doesn't believe in the specific fact that Mohammed is a prophet of God.
sentences.zh: 没有任何尝试去解释对于一个不相信上帝、不相信天使，甚至不相信穆罕默德是上帝先知这一特定事实的人来说，这可能意味着什么。

sentences.en: And likewise, this is this is something that you will find in books by very, very reputable academics.
sentences.zh: 同样，你在一些非常非常权威的学者写的书中也会发现这一点。

sentences.en: So there's a book written by Glenn Bowersock, very distinguished ancient historian who wrote a book called The Crucible of Islam, which is, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如格伦·鲍尔索克写的一本书，他是一位非常杰出的古代史学家，写了一本名为《伊斯兰的熔炉》的书，这本书，你知道的，

sentences.en: full of brilliant analysis of of religious traditions.
sentences.zh: 充满了对宗教传统的精彩分析。

sentences.en: I mean, he does a brilliantly kind of skeptical account of the traditional accounts of the fall of Jerusalem to the Persians and the way that the Romans take it back.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对关于耶路撒冷陷落于波斯人手中以及罗马人夺回耶路撒冷方式的传统叙述，做出了非常精彩的怀疑论解读。

sentences.en: But when he's writing about Mohammed, he's got this bold line.
sentences.zh: 但当他写到穆罕默德时，他写了这样一句大胆的话。

sentences.en: The revelations that Gabriel brought to Mohammed came in Mecca.
sentences.zh: 加百列带给穆罕默德的启示是在麦加降临的。

sentences.en: He doesn't elaborate on that.
sentences.zh: 他没有对此进行详细阐述。

sentences.en: He's asking, you know, he's saying Mohammed gets it from an angel and leaves it at that.
sentences.zh: 他是在问，你知道的，他说穆罕默德从天使那里得到了启示，然后就到此为止了。

sentences.en: Well, this is a bit like when I did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点像我做的那样。

sentences.en: So when I did that course, the Near East in the Age of Justine and Mohammed, I remember saying to my tutor, not about the Islamic element, but actually about icons.
sentences.zh: 当我上那门课《查士丁尼和穆罕默德时代的近东》时，我记得我对导师说，不是关于伊斯兰元素，而是关于圣像。

sentences.en: There was a point at which a source says an icon repelled an army or something.
sentences.zh: 有一个地方，资料说圣像击退了一支军队之类的。

sentences.en: And I said, but surely I don't.
sentences.zh: 我说，但我肯定不相信。

sentences.en: I'm not meant to believe that.
sentences.zh: 我不应该相信那个吧。

sentences.en: What problem, I think?
sentences.zh: 我想，有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you don't have a problem as a historian saying that an icon can't repel an army or you don't believe that Jesus could do miracles or you don't believe, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为历史学家，你说圣像不能击退军队，或者你不相信耶稣能行神迹，或者你不相信，你知道的，

sentences.en: in the acts of the every word of the acts of the apostles.
sentences.zh: 《使徒行传》里的每一个字，这并没有什么问题。

sentences.en: But it is more difficult for a historian to say that of early Islam because you're worried about giving offence effectively.
sentences.zh: 但历史学家要对早期伊斯兰教说同样的话就更困难了，因为你担心会造成冒犯。

sentences.en: Effectively, but also I think it's not just offence, but I think upsetting people for whom the Quran is the revelation that's come from God.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但我认为不仅仅是冒犯，我认为还会让那些视《古兰经》为上帝启示的人感到不安。

sentences.en: And if you start putting it on the slab of historical inquiry and dissecting it and chopping it up and measuring it against other things,
sentences.zh: 如果你开始把它放在历史探究的案板上，解剖它、切碎它，并用其他事物来衡量它，

sentences.en: then obviously that's a stressful thing to do.
sentences.zh: 那么显然这是一件令人压力很大的事情。

sentences.en: But I think that's not a reason not to do it because I'm sure, you know, I mean, I know for a fact that most Muslims are happy to accept that if you're not a Muslim, then,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这不是不做的理由，因为我确定，你知道的，我确信大多数穆斯林乐于接受这一点：如果你不是穆斯林，那么，

sentences.en: of course, you have to arrive in an alternative explanation for where the Quran comes from.
sentences.zh: 当然，你必须为《古兰经》的来源找到一个替代的解释。

sentences.en: And I think there are explanations for where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为对于它的来源是有解释的。

sentences.en: And I think they're not divorced from Mohammed.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它们并非与穆罕默德毫无关联。

sentences.en: So we'll come to that after the break.
sentences.zh: 所以我们休息之后再谈这个。

sentences.en: Let's come back after the break.
sentences.zh: 让我们休息之后回来。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的余韵》。

sentences.en: We are talking about the life of Mohammed and early Islam.
sentences.zh: 我们正在讨论穆罕默德的生平和早期伊斯兰教。

sentences.en: And Tom Holland, you posed before the break this question about the Quran or where the Quran comes from.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德，你在休息前提出了关于《古兰经》或《古兰经》来源的问题。

sentences.en: So there are Quranic fragments, aren't there, which have been carbon dated.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一些《古兰经》残片，对吧，已经经过了碳定年法检测。

sentences.en: So there is one in Birmingham, I think it is.
sentences.zh: 伯明翰有一份，我想是这样。

sentences.en: Let me get my notes.
sentences.zh: 让我找找我的笔记。

sentences.en: The Birmingham fragment is no later than the 640s or so.
sentences.zh: 伯明翰残片不晚于640年代左右。

sentences.en: There's one in Tübingen in Germany, 650s or 660s.
sentences.zh: 德国图宾根有一份，是650年代或660年代的。

sentences.en: So we know that something that elements of the Quran...
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，《古兰经》的一些元素……

sentences.en: Even they are problematic because that's the latest date.
sentences.zh: 即使是这些也存在问题，因为那是较晚的日期。

sentences.en: The earlier dates are well into the 6th century, so before supposedly Mohammed has been born.
sentences.zh: 较早的日期是在6世纪，也就是在穆罕默德被认为出生之前。

sentences.en: So that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个问题。

sentences.en: And the obvious suggestion, the obvious solution to that is that it's the manuscript, it's the parchment that's being tested, not the ink.
sentences.zh: 而显而易见的建议，显而易见的解决方案是，被测试的是手稿，是羊皮纸，而不是墨水。

sentences.en: So this could be fragments.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是残片。

sentences.en: The problem is whenever you are trying to find absolute kind of solidity, absolute certainty in this field, it's like wading through sinking sands.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，每当你试图在这个领域寻找绝对的稳固、绝对的确定性时，就像在流沙中跋涉一样。

sentences.en: And every time you think you found kind of solid ground, you found it giving it away again.
sentences.zh: 每当你以为自己找到了坚实的地面，却发现它又塌陷了。

sentences.en: It gives away again.
sentences.zh: 它又塌陷了。

sentences.en: But historians of the Quran generally believe, don't they, that the Quran was, as it were, sort of enshrined.
sentences.zh: 但《古兰经》的历史学家通常认为，对吧，《古兰经》是，怎么说呢，被供奉起来的。

sentences.en: It was set in stone, as it were, later.
sentences.zh: 它是在后来被刻在石头上的，可以这么说。

sentences.en: That there were bits of it that possibly come from...
sentences.zh: 其中有一些片段可能来自……

sentences.en: There were different versions of the same passage, for example, at different points in the text.
sentences.zh: 例如，在文本的不同地方，同一段落有不同的版本。

sentences.en: That the text was edited at some point after Mohammed's death.
sentences.zh: 文本在穆罕默德去世后的某个时间点被编辑过。

sentences.en: That must be the case.
sentences.zh: 那一定是事实。

sentences.en: There are probably as many different versions of how and why the Quran emerged the way it did, as there are historians writing about it.
sentences.zh: 关于《古兰经》是如何以及为什么以这种方式出现的，可能存在着和研究它的历史学家一样多的不同版本。

sentences.en: In fact, I thought that this would come up.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想到这可能会被提出来。

sentences.en: So I armed myself with a copy of a book called The Quran and its historical context.
sentences.zh: 所以我准备了一本名为《古兰经及其历史背景》的书。

sentences.en: And it's an introductory essay by the great scholar of early Islam, Fred Donner, who's at Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这是一篇由伟大的早期伊斯兰学者弗雷德·唐纳撰写的导论文章，他在芝加哥大学。

sentences.en: And I'll read it.
sentences.zh: 我会读一下。

sentences.en: It's a paragraph, but I think it's worth reading because this is the perspective of an absolutely accepted, standard-bearing scholar of this subject.
sentences.zh: 这是一个段落，但我认为值得一读，因为这是该领域一位绝对被认可的、标杆性的学者的观点。

sentences.en: And he opens it by saying,
sentences.zh: 他开篇说道，

sentences.en: Quranic studies as a field of academic research appears today to be in a state of disarray.
sentences.zh: 作为学术研究领域的《古兰经》研究，今天似乎处于混乱状态。

sentences.en: Those of us who study Islam's origins have to admit collectively that we simply do not know some very basic things about the Quran.
sentences.zh: 我们这些研究伊斯兰起源的人必须共同承认，我们对《古兰经》的一些非常基本的事情一无所知。

sentences.en: Things so basic that the knowledge of them is usually taken for granted by scholars dealing with other texts.
sentences.zh: 这些事情太基本了，以至于处理其他文本的学者通常认为这些知识是理所当然的。

sentences.en: They include such questions as, how did the Quran originate?
sentences.zh: 它们包括诸如，《古兰经》是如何起源的？

sentences.en: Where did it come from?
sentences.zh: 它从哪里来？

sentences.en: And when did it first appear?
sentences.zh: 它是什么时候首次出现的？

sentences.en: How was it first written?
sentences.zh: 它是如何首次被书写的？

sentences.en: In what kind of language was, is it written?
sentences.zh: 它是用什么样的语言书写的？

sentences.en: What form did it take?
sentences.zh: 它采取了什么形式？

sentences.en: Who constituted its first audience?
sentences.zh: 谁构成了它最初的受众？

sentences.en: How is it transmitted from one generation to another, especially in its early years?
sentences.zh: 它是如何从一代传给下一代的，特别是在它早期的岁月里？

sentences.en: When, how, and by whom was it codified?
sentences.zh: 它是什么时候、如何以及由谁编纂成典的？

sentences.en: Those familiar with the Quran and the scholarship on it will know that to ask even one of these questions immediately plunges us into realms of grave uncertainty and has the potential to spark intense debate.
sentences.zh: 熟悉《古兰经》及其学术研究的人会知道，提出这些问题中的任何一个，都会立即将我们带入充满严重不确定性的领域，并有可能引发激烈的辩论。

sentences.en: Which is, you know, putting it mildly.
sentences.zh: 这，你知道的，说得委婉一点。

sentences.en: It's a very good way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种很好的表达方式。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, because the traditional account of Muhammad's life is the only version that we have, the moment you question that or you move away from that, essentially,
sentences.zh: 所以，因为关于穆罕默德生平的传统叙述是我们拥有的唯一版本，当你质疑这一点或偏离这一点时，本质上，

sentences.en: you have to construct a model for what might have happened.
sentences.zh: 你必须构建一个关于可能发生了什么的模型。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That, you know, you're putting fragments together.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你是在拼凑碎片。

sentences.en: You're trying to put together a jigsaw puzzle in which large bits are missing.
sentences.zh: 你是在试图拼凑一个缺失了大部分碎片的拼图。

sentences.en: And you can't even be certain what the jigsaw puzzle originally looked like.
sentences.zh: 而且你甚至无法确定这个拼图最初看起来是什么样子的。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising that basically there are as many different accounts of how and why the Quran might have emerged and how that might relate to Muhammad and how Muhammad might relate to the context of late antiquity as there are scholars writing about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于《古兰经》是如何以及为什么可能出现，以及它可能与穆罕默德有何关联，以及穆罕默德可能与古典时代晚期的背景有何关联，存在着和研究它的学者一样多的不同叙述，这也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: And that is what makes this, I think, uniquely challenging to study.
sentences.zh: 而这正是使它，我认为，在研究上具有独特挑战性的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, that's why I basically, the five years I spent on this, my brain ached the whole time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是为什么我基本上，我花在这上面的五年里，我的大脑一直都在痛。

sentences.en: But when you finish, so your book is The Shadow of the Sword, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但当你完成时，你的书是《剑的阴影》，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, fascinating book.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，引人入胜的书。

sentences.en: And you did a TV program or two programs, I think.
sentences.zh: 你还做了一个电视节目或两个节目，我想。

sentences.en: Was it two programs?
sentences.zh: 是两个节目吗？

sentences.en: Just one.
sentences.zh: 只有一个。

sentences.en: Just one.
sentences.zh: 只有一个。

sentences.en: Accompanying it.
sentences.zh: 随书附带的。

sentences.en: You know, incredibly rich subject that you clearly had great, you know, fun doing, although it was a challenge.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一个极其丰富的主题，你显然在做的时候很有，你知道的，乐趣，尽管这是一个挑战。

sentences.en: But you must have come out of it with a sense, however provisional, that you, you know, if I put you on the spot and said, what do you think the story is?
sentences.zh: 但你从中走出来时，一定有一种感觉，无论多么初步，如果你让我当场回答，你认为故事是什么？

sentences.en: What would you say?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I think the Muhammad was a merchant.
sentences.zh: 我认为穆罕默德是一位商人。

sentences.en: So I think that part of the tradition is true.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为传统中的那部分是真实的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, we told that by this very early source that you mentioned.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们提到的那个非常早期的文献里就是这么说的。

sentences.en: He sees himself as standing in the line of Abrahamic prophets.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己处于亚伯拉罕诸先知的行列之中。

sentences.en: So he's probably got that because Judaism is floating around Mecca or the Arabian Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 所以他很可能拥有这种认知，因为犹太教当时在麦加或阿拉伯半岛随处可见。

sentences.en: It's the ideas of, there's a sort of, there's a sort of stew of ideas.
sentences.zh: 这是一种思想，怎么说呢，就像是一个思想的大熔炉。

sentences.en: Come to that in a minute, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 或许待会儿再谈这个。

sentences.en: Come to that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 待会儿再谈这个。

sentences.en: Things that we can be certain about.
sentences.zh: 我们可以确定的事情。

sentences.en: He, I think he, he, he engages in a hijra, an exodus.
sentences.zh: 我认为他参与了希吉拉，也就是一次出走。

sentences.en: I think the ideal of the kind of emigration is, is fundamental to his history and to, to the Quran.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种移民的理想，对于他的历史以及《古兰经》来说是根本性的。

sentences.en: So I think that's, that's, I think that, um, Yathrib is where he sets up a community.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，嗯，雅特里布就是他建立社群的地方。

sentences.en: Um, and that's both because Yathrib is, is repeatedly mentioned in the contemporary sources by, you know, bishops or whoever who have no particular reason to, to,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这既是因为雅特里布在当时的文献中被反复提及，无论是主教还是其他人，他们都没有特别的理由去，去，

sentences.en: to lie about that, to distort that.
sentences.zh: 去撒谎，去歪曲事实。

sentences.en: Um, and, and also because, um, in, uh, the earliest biographies, Muslim biographies of Muhammad, there are preserved fragments of,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，也是因为，在最早的传记，即穆斯林的穆罕默德传记中，保留了一些片段，

sentences.en: of what's conventionally called the constitution of Medina, which is clearly very early texts.
sentences.zh: 也就是通常所说的《麦地那宪章》，这显然是非常早期的文本。

sentences.en: That's a state building kind of exercise.
sentences.zh: 那是一种国家建设性质的实践。

sentences.en: Yes, state building.
sentences.zh: 是的，国家建设。

sentences.en: So I think that, um, Yathrib is clearly central.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，嗯，雅特里布显然处于核心地位。

sentences.en: Central, as you said, there are inscriptions that do seem to kind of tie in with, with some of the Muslim accounts about this that have been found.
sentences.zh: 核心地位，正如你所说，确实有一些铭文似乎与穆斯林关于此事的记载相吻合。

sentences.en: Um, I think that this community, um, was interested in expanding.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这个社群，嗯，是有意扩张的。

sentences.en: I think it had a kind of, um, a kind of post-biblical vision that it was interested in spreading.
sentences.zh: 我认为它有一种，嗯，一种后圣经时代的愿景，它有兴趣传播这种愿景。

sentences.en: I think Muhammad led the invasion, um, of Palestine.
sentences.zh: 我认为穆罕默德领导了对巴勒斯坦的入侵。

sentences.en: I think that he died and I think that his body was taken back to Medina.
sentences.zh: 我认为他去世了，而且我认为他的遗体被带回了麦地那。

sentences.en: And I think that, um, he then essentially got forgotten for a bit and we'll come to the reasons why for that perhaps a bit later.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，嗯，他后来基本上被遗忘了一段时间，我们稍后可能会谈到其中的原因。

sentences.en: But, but the, the issue then is if he's lead, if he's founding this, this biblically enthused, informed community, um, where does his knowledge of, of the Bible come from?
sentences.zh: 但是，问题在于，如果他是在领导，如果他是在建立这个充满圣经色彩、受圣经启发的社群，那么他关于圣经的知识是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: Well, at least his biblical traditions, if, as the tradition says, he's growing up in Mecca, which is an entirely pagan city, you know,
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少是他的圣经传统，如果按照传统说法，他在麦加长大，那可是一个完全异教的城市，你知道，

sentences.en: a thousand miles away from where Christians and Jews are.
sentences.zh: 距离基督徒和犹太人居住的地方有一千英里远。

sentences.en: And it seems to me that the story of, of Muhammad growing up in Mecca or what the place we now call Mecca is the equivalent of Christians saying that Jesus is the son of, of,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，关于穆罕默德在麦加长大的故事，或者我们现在称之为麦加的地方，等同于基督徒说耶稣是，嗯，

sentences.en: of a virgin.
sentences.zh: 童贞女之子。

sentences.en: That in both cases, it's an attempt to insulate the vehicle of the divine in the case of Muhammad, the, the, you know, the essence of the divine in the case of Jesus from the, the,
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，这都是为了保护神圣的载体——在穆罕默德的例子中，是神圣的本质；在耶稣的例子中，是神圣的本质——免受，嗯，

sentences.en: the charge that they, these are frauds.
sentences.zh: 免受他们是骗子的指控。

sentences.en: That, you know, Jesus is the son of a centurion or something that, you know, Mary got pregnant in perfectly normal manner, uh, or Muhammad that his, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如耶稣是百夫长的儿子，或者玛丽是以完全正常的方式怀孕的，或者穆罕默德，你知道，

sentences.en: he's influenced by the context of the world that he's living in.
sentences.zh: 他受到了他所处世界环境的影响。

sentences.en: And the reason why that has to be guarded against is because it might imply that these traditions, these elements within the Quran might have come from the context of the, of,
sentences.zh: 之所以必须防范这种说法，是因为它可能暗示这些传统，即《古兰经》中的这些元素，可能来自穆罕默德出生时所处的更广阔的世界背景。

sentences.en: of the broader world in which Muhammad has been born.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是历史与信仰之间产生冲突的地方，因为如果你是一个信徒，

sentences.en: Now that of course is, you know, this, this is where the tension between history and belief kind of locks horns because if, if you're, if you're a believer,
sentences.zh: 那么当然，这一切都来自上帝。

sentences.en: then of course it comes from God.
sentences.zh: 这就是你信仰的本质。

sentences.en: That's, that's the essence of your belief.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不是信徒，那么当然，你会说，看看这些文本，你知道，里面有所有这些元素。

sentences.en: But if you're not a believer, then of course, you know, you're going to say, well, look at this text, you know, there are all these elements.
sentences.zh: 它们显然来自基督教、犹太教，甚至往往是更古老的传统。

sentences.en: They, they clearly come from Christian, Jewish, often, you know, even older traditions.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须问自己，穆罕默德是如何以及为什么吸收了这些东西？

sentences.en: And then you have to ask yourself, well, how and why did they, did Muhammad come to, to absorb them?
sentences.zh: 所以，其中一个关键词，显然这里面的关键点在于麦加，即麦加在其中扮演了什么角色，因为麦加是一个贸易城镇。

sentences.en: So, so one of the words, obviously the key things in this is Mecca is the idea is, is what, what, where Mecca fits in because Mecca is a, is a, is a trading town.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它有集市，有市场，人们会去那里。

sentences.en: Um, it has fares, it has markets, it people go.
sentences.zh: 但我们怎么知道这一点呢？

sentences.en: But how do we know that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这，这是我们，这是我们指导性的假设。

sentences.en: Well, um, this is, this is our, this is our guiding assumption anyway.
sentences.zh: 现在，像帕特里夏·克罗内这样的历史学家指出的《古兰经》中的一点，他们说这引发了疑问，那就是穆罕默德谈到，

sentences.en: Now, one of the things that people like historians, like Patricia Croner have pointed to in the Quran that they say they have raises questions is that Muhammad talks,
sentences.zh: 《古兰经》中谈到他的敌人是那些，嗯，他们种植葡萄藤，有枣椰树，有绵羊和牛之类的人。

sentences.en: it talks in the Quran about his foes being people who have, um, they, they grow, you know, vines, they have date palms, they have sheep and cows and things like that.
sentences.zh: 这些东西基本上在麦加可能并不存在，这就有问题了，对吧？

sentences.en: That basically people probably didn't have in Mecca, which is a problem, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是个问题。

sentences.en: Yes, it is a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，一些历史学家说，这表明传统的假设，即这一切都发生在麦加，一定是错误的。

sentences.en: So, so some historians say, well, that suggests that the traditional assumption that all this is happening in Mecca must be wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有所有这些绵羊和牛，那么它一定发生在更北边的地方，

sentences.en: That if they've got all these sheep and cows, it must be happening further north,
sentences.zh: 这会使其更接近巴勒斯坦和罗马世界，而这些思想可能正是从那里传来的。

sentences.en: which would bring it closer to the world of Palestine and the Roman world where the ideas could be coming from.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是橄榄，所提到的那种橄榄只生长在更靠近地中海的地方。

sentences.en: Um, and particularly olives and the, the kind of olive that's referred to is only grown kind of within the much closer to the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是一个问题。

sentences.en: So that's, so, so that's a, I think is a problem.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，杰拉德·霍廷在一本划时代的书中提出的论点也很有道理，即在《古兰经》中被称为“多神论者”的人，

sentences.en: And I think also the, the fact that it was argued by Gerald Horting in a, in a kind of epical book, um, that people who are called the Mushrakin in, uh, in, in the Quran, uh,
sentences.zh: 他们实践着所谓的“以什拉克”，即某种将神灵，或者可能是天使，与上帝联系起来的行为。

sentences.en: who practice what's called Shi'ik, which is kind of associating, um, deities or perhaps angels with, with God.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的罪行。

sentences.en: And this is their crime.
sentences.zh: 嗯，传统说法是，这是异教崇拜，他们崇拜的是来自异教阿拉伯的神和女神。

sentences.en: Um, and the tradition is, is that this is paganism, that they are worshiping gods and goddesses from, you know, pagan Arabia.
sentences.zh: 但霍廷的论点是，嗯，实际上穆罕默德或先知，或者无论《古兰经》的作者是谁，

sentences.en: But Horting's argument is that, um, actually Muhammad or the prophet or whoever the author of the Quran is, is,
sentences.zh: 称他们为偶像崇拜者，就像新教徒可能称天主教徒为偶像崇拜者一样。

sentences.en: is calling them idolaters in the way that the Protestants might call Catholics idolaters.
