sentences.en: And Abdul Malik casts himself as the deputy of God, the caliph.
sentences.zh: 阿卜杜勒·马利克将自己塑造为上帝的代理人，即哈里发。

sentences.en: And seems, you know, I mean, a man of immense self-confidence, pretty convinced that he is as significant a figure as Muhammad himself is.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来，你知道，我的意思是，一个极度自信的人，相当确信自己和穆罕默德本人一样重要。

sentences.en: But he wins in the civil war, defeats Ibn al-Zabiyah, establishes, you know, a kind of a universal rule over the Arab empire.
sentences.zh: 但他赢得了内战，击败了伊本·祖拜尔，确立了，你知道，一种对阿拉伯帝国的普遍统治。

sentences.en: And it's under Abdul Malik that you start to get the massive proclamation of Muhammad as a prophet of God.
sentences.zh: 正是在阿卜杜勒·马利克统治下，你开始看到大规模地宣扬穆罕默德作为上帝的先知。

sentences.en: It seems the codification of the Koran.
sentences.zh: 似乎还有《古兰经》的编纂。

sentences.en: It seems the initial proclamation of the place that we would now call Mecca as having been Mecca, as having been the site of the sanctuary of God.
sentences.zh: 似乎还有最初将我们现在称为麦加的地方宣布为麦加，宣布为上帝圣所的所在地。

sentences.en: And all of this kind of package,
sentences.zh: 所有这一切，

sentences.en: it's from the reign of Abdul Malik that you can start to see something that we will recognize as Islam emerging and taking the form that it's had ever since.
sentences.zh: 正是从阿卜杜勒·马利克的统治时期开始，你可以看到我们所认识的伊斯兰教正在兴起，并形成了它此后一直保持的形式。

sentences.en: And this is at a time, though, Tom, when there would have been people who could remember Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆，这还是在一个人们可能还记得穆罕默德的时代。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, if they were old, they were very old.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果他们老了，那也是非常老了。

sentences.en: So we're talking about you're talking about what, six eighties, did you say or so?
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是，你谈论的是什么，六百八十年代，你是这么说的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if Muhammad died in 632, it's plausible that some old people would or there would be sons of people who certainly could have remembered him.
sentences.zh: 所以如果穆罕默德死于632年，那么一些老人或者那些肯定能记得他的人的后代还活着是合理的。

sentences.en: But equally, they're probably very few.
sentences.zh: 但同样，他们可能非常少。

sentences.en: And so that therefore enables people to kind of, you know, you have a slightly blanker palette than you might otherwise have done.
sentences.zh: 因此，这使得人们能够，你知道，你拥有了一块比你原本可能拥有的更空白的调色板。

sentences.en: You know, and this is this is the Arabs at this stage are not writing stuff down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是，这就是阿拉伯人在这个阶段还没有把事情写下来。

sentences.en: Or if they are, it hasn't survived.
sentences.zh: 或者即使他们写了，也没有流传下来。

sentences.en: They're not writing accounts.
sentences.zh: 他们没有写下记录。

sentences.en: So it's these are all accounts.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是叙述。

sentences.en: And this is an age when basically traditions can be started almost from scratch.
sentences.zh: 这是一个基本上可以从零开始建立传统的时代。

sentences.en: I mean, this is, you know, the famous example is Christians turning up in the Holy Land and kind of identify all these places as the bush, you know, the bush where Moses.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是，你知道，著名的例子是基督徒出现在圣地，并把所有这些地方都认定为灌木丛，你知道，摩西所在的灌木丛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, the burning bush or, you know, this house is where St. Peter lived or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，燃烧的灌木丛，或者，你知道，这所房子是圣彼得住过的地方，等等。

sentences.en: However, the same thing happens with Jewish traditions, the same thing happens with Zoroastrian traditions.
sentences.zh: 然而，同样的事情也发生在犹太传统中，同样的事情也发生在琐罗亚斯德教传统中。

sentences.en: And there seems no reason why the same thing can't can't have happened with with what becomes Muslim traditions.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎没有理由认为同样的事情不会发生在后来成为穆斯林传统的事情上。

sentences.en: Because the truth is, is that the first mention of Mecca isn't until the middle of the 8th century.
sentences.zh: 因为事实是，对麦加的首次提及直到8世纪中叶才出现。

sentences.en: And even then it's placed somewhere in the Fertile Crescent in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 即使在那时，它也被放置在新月沃土的伊拉克某处。

sentences.en: And the location of the House of God, which is clearly crucially important, is presumably where Muhammad went on Hijrah from, is presumably the place that Ibn al-Zabar is going to.
sentences.zh: 而上帝之屋的位置，这显然至关重要，大概是穆罕默德迁徙时去的地方，大概是伊本·祖拜尔要去的地方。

sentences.en: But we're told it gets destroyed.
sentences.zh: 但我们被告知它被摧毁了。

sentences.en: It gets destroyed twice over.
sentences.zh: 它被摧毁了两次。

sentences.en: So if it's been leveled, the task of rebuilding it and perhaps locating it somewhere else in a place that the Emmaids,
sentences.zh: 所以如果它被夷为平地，重建它并可能将其定位在阿拔斯王朝（阿卜杜勒·马利克所属的家族）所在的其他地方的任务，

sentences.en: the family from which Abdul-Malik comes from, becomes much easier.
sentences.zh: 就变得容易多了。

sentences.en: And I don't think that it would be a kind of deliberate fraud.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是一种蓄意的欺诈。

sentences.en: It's just, you know, rather like, you know, Olympus was a place that kind of lots of identified with lots of mountains
sentences.zh: 这只是，你知道，就像，你知道，奥林匹斯山是一个被许多人与许多山联系在一起的地方，

sentences.en: before it settled on the mountain we now call Olympus or Camelot.
sentences.zh: 在它最终确定为我们现在称为奥林匹斯山或卡米洛特之前。

sentences.en: You know, lots of locations for Camelot.
sentences.zh: 你知道，卡米洛特有很多位置。

sentences.en: But there are lots of places, lots of different traditions, perhaps associated with Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 但有很多地方，许多不同的传统，也许与穆罕默德有关。

sentences.en: Perhaps Muhammad did have an association with the place that comes to be Mecca.
sentences.zh: 也许穆罕默德确实与后来成为麦加的地方有联系。

sentences.en: But essentially, it's a time, these decades from, you know, the lifetime of Muhammad through the kind of 50 years that follow are a period where everything is up for grabs
sentences.zh: 但本质上，这是一个时代，从穆罕默德的一生到随后的50年，这些几十年是一个一切皆有可能的时期，

sentences.en: and the concrete is not yet set and the guy who shapes and moulds the story.
sentences.zh: 混凝土尚未凝固，而那个塑造和塑造故事的人。

sentences.en: So I think there's a question somewhere about, you know, is there someone who's equivalent of St. Paul?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为某个地方有一个问题，你知道，是否有人相当于圣保罗？

sentences.en: I mean, basically, Abdul-Malik is the equivalent of St. Paul and Constantine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，阿卜杜勒·马利克就是圣保罗和君士坦丁的等同物。

sentences.en: He's the person who is establishing Muhammad as the prophet of a god who has also given his sanction to the rule of Abdul-Malik and the Arabs over the empire of the world,
sentences.zh: 他是一个将穆罕默德确立为上帝先知的人，这位上帝也认可了阿卜杜勒·马利克和阿拉伯人对世界帝国的统治，

sentences.en: but who is also kind of canonising the story of Muhammad, the story of his relationship to a shrine
sentences.zh: 但他也在某种程度上将穆罕默德的故事、他与圣所关系的故事，

sentences.en: and the story of his relationship to the Koran in a way that will then endure and pass down.
sentences.zh: 以及他与《古兰经》关系的故事神圣化了，以一种将持续并传承下去的方式。

sentences.en: And the early, you know, the early accounts get erased.
sentences.zh: 而早期的，你知道，早期的记录被抹去了。

sentences.en: Before we, we've already talked for probably far too long, but before we come to an end, let's just talk a little bit about Muhammad's reputation later.
sentences.zh: 在我们，我们已经谈了太久了，但在结束之前，让我们谈谈穆罕默德后来的声誉。

sentences.en: So Muhammad obviously has run, you know, he's a figure who has resounded through history, not just for Muslims, but for non-Muslims too.
sentences.zh: 所以穆罕默德显然已经，你知道，他是一个在历史上引起共鸣的人物，不仅对穆斯林，对非穆斯林也是如此。

sentences.en: And I know you've got a couple of good examples of people who wrote about Muhammad afterwards.
sentences.zh: 我知道你有一些关于后来写穆罕默德的人的好例子。

sentences.en: So Carlisle, I think, is one of your examples, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以卡莱尔，我想是你例子中的一个，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, before that, for Christians, they have no sense of Muhammad as a prophet or a founder of a different religious tradition.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在此之前，对于基督徒来说，他们没有把穆罕默德视为先知或不同宗教传统的创始人的概念。

sentences.en: They see him as a schismatic.
sentences.zh: 他们视他为分裂主义者。

sentences.en: So in Dante, that's the fate he's sentenced to be torn to pieces, reassembled and torn to pieces again.
sentences.zh: 所以在但丁的作品中，他的命运是被判处撕成碎片，重新组装，然后再撕成碎片。

sentences.en: At what point, Tom, did people stop thinking of Islam as a sort of, did Christians, sort of Romans, at what point did they stop thinking of Islam?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，人们在什么时候停止把伊斯兰教视为一种，基督徒，罗马人，在什么时候他们停止把伊斯兰教视为……

sentences.en: Because at first they clearly thought of Islam as this sort of weird Jewish heresy, exactly.
sentences.zh: 因为起初他们显然把伊斯兰教视为一种奇怪的犹太异端，没错。

sentences.en: But at what point did they say it's not, it's a religion in its own right that's got a rich tradition and all this sort of stuff?
sentences.zh: 但他们是在什么时候说它不是，它是一个拥有丰富传统等等的独立宗教？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's into the beginning of the early modern period.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是进入近代早期的时候。

sentences.en: And then through the Victorian period, people get fascinated by Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 然后通过维多利亚时代，人们对穆罕默德着迷。

sentences.en: So as you say, Carlisle writes a life of him and kind of enshrines him as the model of a great man.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，卡莱尔写了他的传记，并把他奉为伟人的典范。

sentences.en: And then you also have other historians who kind of try and do the life and times style approach.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有其他历史学家，他们试图采用生平时代风格的方法。

sentences.en: So putting Muhammad in the context of the age.
sentences.zh: 所以把穆罕默德放在那个时代的背景下。

sentences.en: But that's where you get all the traditions of him as a merchant living and Mecca as a kind of great merchant city
sentences.zh: 但这就是你得到所有关于他作为商人的传统，以及麦加作为一个伟大的商业城市，

sentences.en: and all this kind of thing, which then gets picked up by Muslim scholars.
sentences.zh: 以及所有这类事情的地方，这些后来被穆斯林学者所采纳。

sentences.en: So there's a sense in which the model of Muhammad today is quite a westernized one.
sentences.zh: 所以某种意义上，今天的穆罕默德模型相当西化。

sentences.en: And there are lots of Muslims, of course, who recognize that and who want to go back to an original, you know, strip away, get out the paint stripper.
sentences.zh: 当然，有很多穆斯林认识到这一点，并希望回到最初，你知道，剥离，拿出脱漆剂。

sentences.en: But there's a brilliant description of what they're doing by a scholar called Keita Ali, who's written a wonderful book about the afterlife of Muhammad
sentences.zh: 但有一位叫基塔·阿里（Keita Ali）的学者对他们所做的事情有精彩的描述，他写了一本关于穆罕默德身后事的精彩著作，

sentences.en: and the way that both Muslims and non-Muslims have understood him.
sentences.zh: 以及穆斯林和非穆斯林理解他的方式。

sentences.en: And it says about the text written symbolically came to be read literally.
sentences.zh: 书中说，象征性书写的文本后来被字面解读了。

sentences.en: And I think that's that's the problem is that there's so much about Muhammad that gets is now taken as a kind of literary, literal historical account in the Muslim tradition.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是问题所在，关于穆罕默德有太多东西现在在穆斯林传统中被视为一种文学性的、字面上的历史记录。

sentences.en: Whereas, in fact, it for most of Islamic history, Muhammad is that, you know, he's the beloved of God.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实上，在大多数伊斯兰历史中，穆罕默德是那个，你知道，他是上帝的挚爱。

sentences.en: He's the man who.
sentences.zh: 他是那个人。

sentences.en: That's why he's loved.
sentences.zh: 这就是他被爱的原因。

sentences.en: And the kind of attempt to see him as a historical figure is much more of a western project.
sentences.zh: 而试图将他视为历史人物的尝试更多是一个西方项目。

sentences.en: So there is a kind of tension there, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那里存在一种张力。

sentences.en: And it's one that obviously is focused in western countries.
sentences.zh: 而且这显然在西方国家很突出。

sentences.en: It's a quest for the historical Jesus, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是对历史耶稣的探索，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's very not dissimilar.
sentences.zh: 非常相似。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yes.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，是的。

sentences.en: You know, the attempt to historicize ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，将基督历史化的尝试。

sentences.en: And so that whole tradition, in a way, is a kind of Christian one, because it's bred of the Christian desire to make sense of Jesus and the Bible historically.
sentences.zh: 所以整个传统，在某种程度上，是一种基督教传统，因为它源于基督徒从历史上理解耶稣和《圣经》的愿望。

sentences.en: And people then using those techniques, then apply it to the Muslim tradition, which is why.
sentences.zh: 然后人们使用这些技术，将其应用于穆斯林传统，这就是为什么。

sentences.en: I mean, inevitably, I think it kind of can raise hackles among Muslims because you're applying an alien tradition.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不可避免地，我认为这可能会引起穆斯林的反感，因为你正在应用一种外来的传统。

sentences.en: And I'm permanently in awe of your ability to, no matter what the subject, to seamlessly make a very convincing argument that it all comes back to your excellent book, Dominion,
sentences.zh: 我一直对你的能力感到敬畏，无论主题是什么，都能天衣无缝地提出一个非常有说服力的论点，即这一切都回到了你那本关于基督教传统的优秀著作《统治》（Dominion）上，

sentences.en: about the Christian tradition.
sentences.zh: 关于基督教传统。

sentences.en: There you are.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: I've done the plug for you.
sentences.zh: 我已经为你做了宣传。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: If only I could find a way to link all subjects to the second premiership of Harold Wilson in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 如果我能找到一种方法把所有主题都联系到1970年代哈罗德·威尔逊的第二个首相任期就好了。

sentences.en: But, of course, when and if you come to write your book on the latter years of the Thatcher premiership and into the major premiership, I hope you'll do that.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，当你写关于撒切尔首相任期后期到梅杰首相任期的书时，我希望你会这样做。

sentences.en: Then, of course,
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，

sentences.en: debates over the relationship of the historical Mohammed to how people have interpreted or misinterpreted him absolutely becomes a part of contemporary British history.
sentences.zh: 关于历史上的穆罕默德与人们如何解释或误解他之间的关系的辩论，绝对成为了当代英国历史的一部分。

sentences.en: You've got the Stannic Verses and you've got everything that follows on from that.
sentences.zh: 你有《撒旦诗篇》，还有随之而来的一切。

sentences.en: So I hope that you too will engage with this fascinating topic.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你也参与这个迷人的话题。

sentences.en: The quest for the historic Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 寻找历史上的玛格丽特·撒切尔。

sentences.en: Well, that's a religious subject.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一个宗教主题。

sentences.en: To turn to on another occasion.
sentences.zh: 留待下次讨论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢。

sentences.en: We'd love to hear your comments.
sentences.zh: 我们很乐意听到你的评论。

sentences.en: What are we doing next time, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们下次做什么？

sentences.en: We're doing Magna Carta, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我们要做《大宪章》。

sentences.en: So King John's Partisans will have very strong views about that.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰王的拥护者对此会有非常强烈的看法。

sentences.en: And let's hope we don't get cancelled for it.
sentences.zh: 希望我们不会因此被取消。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余韵》（The Rest Is History）。
